context: Naoko tells Hina about a moment in her past when she was stubborn but right.
purpose: Aunt sharing personal lesson story with teen.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: ひな、頑固って、悪くないで。
lines.en: Hina, being stubborn isn't a bad thing.
lines.style: Warm, philosophical Kansai accent. Unhurried, like she's sharing something true. Soft weight on the insight, not pushing it. The voice of someone who's lived long enough to know.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.style: Surprised but hopeful. High opening on the question, eyes brightening. Soft, genuine — not performing interest, actually hearing something she needed to hear.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 若い時、皆に反対された。
lines.en: When I was young, everyone told me not to.
lines.style: Nostalgic, matter-of-fact Kansai drawl. Looking back with acceptance, not bitterness. Pace steady and unhurried — the comfort of having survived it.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.style: Leaning in, genuinely curious. Soft and open — the way a child listens when an adult stops performing and starts remembering. Eager but not demanding.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.en: I believed in myself and kept going.
lines.style: Firmer now, grounded. Light conviction on 「信じて」. Kansai warmth still there but with a spine to it — not proud in a loud way, proud in a quiet one.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.style: Hopeful question, soft and tentative. Seeking confirmation that stubbornness can actually work. The voice of an eight-year-old who wants to believe the best thing she's heard all week.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.en: Yeah. I'm proud of who I became.
lines.style: Warm affirmation, genuine Kansai ease. 「誇りに思う」 lands with quiet certainty, not boasting. Tender and complete — the voice of someone who's made peace with her own path.
